ME3600 Classical Control

MATLAB examples and demos of the course, by chapter. Click a file to download it, or run the demo in the browser (no MATLAB needed): all browser demos.

Routh Hurwitz

  • Ball on Plate

    Keep the ball on the green target by tilting the plate yourself, then hand it to C(s). The same controller acts on the x and y axes.

    Run in the browser
    • BOP_Control_Design.m
    • BOP_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Car Steering

    The car drives at constant speed and changes lane every 8 s. The controller steers the front wheels.

    Run in the browser
    • CAR_Control_Design.m
    • CAR_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Cold Storage

    The AC cools the room to a temperature that changes every 6 s. It can only cool, so P ≥ 0.

    Run in the browser
    • CS_Control_Design.m
    • CS_Realtime_Demo.m

  • DC Motor

    The shaft follows a commanded angle that changes every 2 s.

    Run in the browser
    • DCM_Control_Design.m
    • DCM_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Highwire Artist

    The artist stands on the wire and balances with a pole. Try it yourself, then hand it to C(s).

    Run in the browser
    • HA_Control_Design.m
    • HA_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Inverted Pendulum

    Keep the pendulum upright. It starts tilted by 5°; push it to test the controller.

    Run in the browser
    • IP_Control_Design.m
    • IP_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Inverted Pendulum on Cart

    Keep the pendulum upright by pushing the cart. Try it yourself, then hand it to C(s). The view follows the cart.

    Run in the browser
    • IPC_Control_Design.m
    • IPC_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Mass Spring Damper

    A force u moves the mass to a target position that changes every 4 s.

    Run in the browser
    • MSD_Control_Design.m
    • MSD_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Pendulum

    The pendulum hangs from a pivot and is driven to a commanded angle that changes every 4 s.

    Run in the browser
    • PEN_Control_Design.m
    • PEN_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Satellite

    Thrusters turn the satellite to an orientation that changes every 6 s. No friction, no gravity.

    Run in the browser
    • SAT_Control_Design.m
    • SAT_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Two Mass System

    A force on mass 1 moves it to a commanded position; mass 2 swings on the spring between them.

    Run in the browser
    • TM_Control_Design.m
    • TM_Realtime_Demo.m

  • Water Tank

    The inflow fills the tank to a level that changes every 20 s. The tank is drawn to scale. Try 5× speed.

    Run in the browser
    • WT_Control_Design.m
    • WT_Realtime_Demo.m

Frequency Response

  • Mass Spring Damper (Second Order)

    A sinusoidal force pushes the mass. Slow forcing: the mass follows the dashed block (F/k). Near ωn: resonance. Fast forcing: the mass barely moves, opposite to the force.

    Run in the browser
    • FR_MSD_Demo.m

  • Muffled Song

    Hear a Bode plot. A jungle track plays in a loop through G(s). Lower the corner frequency and the hats and cymbals fade while the bass stays: the song sounds as if behind a wall.

    Run in the browser
    • FR_Filter_Coeffs.m
    • FR_Make_Jungle_Track.m
    • FR_Muffled_Song_Demo.m
    • jungle_loop.wav

  • Servo (First Order)

    A sinusoidal voltage drives the motor. At low frequency the speed follows (×K, in phase); above the corner 1/τ it shrinks and lags by up to 90°.

    Run in the browser
    • FR_Servo_Demo.m

  • Spring Damper (High Pass)

    You move the end of a damper; a spring holds the plate. Slow motion: the damper slides and the plate stays (high-pass). Fast motion: the damper acts like a rod and the plate follows.

    Run in the browser
    • FR_SpringDamper_Demo.m
